text:
Maya: heads up — onboarding new zulu-13B q4 model, ran perf harness at 120rps for 30m and p95 jitter is all over the place
Liam: can you paste the run config? was this with kvcache enabled?
Maya: kvcache=on, dynamic_batching=auto, max_batch_size=64, seq_dist: mean 96, var 12
Jordan: did you pin cpu/gpu affinity? last time the noise came from host level contention
Maya: dedicated GPU, no other jobs. logs show spikes aligning with periodic gc in runner
Sara: can you share runner logs around a spike? also which metric definition are you using for p95? we had a mismatch earlier where 'inflight_latency' excluded queue time
Maya: attaching snippet: ```json
{"batching":{"mode":"auto","max_batch_size":64},"cache":{"prefix":true}}
```
ci-bot: perf-harness-job/472 finished — artifacts at https://ci.redwood/perf/472
Liam: thanks — looking at artifacts now
Liam: root cause looks like our 'service_latency_ms' in dashboard was using host->start instead of request->start, so queue latency omitted
Jordan: oof, that explains 30-40ms gap
Maya: also saw cost-per-token calc in /perf-cost dashboard drop when quantize=int8 applied, but CPU encoding variance messed numbers up
Noreen: quick fix: change metric mapping -> 'end_to_end_latency' = timestamp.response_ready - timestamp.request_received
Sara: for CI gate, let's add a synthetic workload with fixed seq length and a second with high variance to catch this
Liam: propose adding two checks: steady-state p95 under fixed seq and p95 ratio(var/steady) < 1.3
Maya: will open PR with test harness changes and updated dashboard mapping
Maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood/perf-harness/pull/128
Jordan: add a short log assertion to fail if batch window increases > 10ms unexpectedly — caught this before
ops: heads-up — if this triggers we'll automatically scale up, that might mask the regression, consider running on capped capacity
Sara: good point — CI should run at reserved capacity to surface real SLO issues
Maya: agreed, will add env var PERF_CAPACITY=reserved in CI job
Liam: I pushed a tiny runner patch to stabilize batch window timer, @Maya can you try a quick re-run?
Maya: re-run started, sharing baseline once done
ci-bot: perf-harness-job/473 queued
Maya: initial 5m looks much better, p95 stable. I'll let it run full 30m and post results
Jordan: nice — once merged let's update the dashboard tooltip to explain what the latency metric includes
Maya: will do. thanks team :thumbsup:
